sources.title: Britain sanctions Sudanese commanders over weaponised rape
UK sanctions Sudanese military leaders implicated in El Fasher ‘campaign of rape’

en.title: UK sanctions 15 Sudanese commanders over alleged rape campaign
en.dek: Britain imposes travel bans and asset freezes on 15 Sudanese military leaders for sexual violence during El Fasher siege.
facts: According to the UK Foreign Office, 15 commanders from RSF and SAF were sanctioned.
The sanctions include travel bans and asset freezes.
The UK allocated £5m to support survivors of sexual violence and £10m for humanitarian aid.
Ed Miliband said perpetrators must be held accountable.
Amnesty International reports 14 million displaced since the war began in April 2023.
body: The United Kingdom announced sanctions on 15 Sudanese commanders on 26 October 2026.
The Foreign Office said the measures target individuals from the Rapid Support Forces and the Sudanese Armed Forces.
Sanctions include travel bans and asset freezes.
The aim is to hold those responsible for war crimes accountable.
The sanctions were issued after UK‑funded investigations by the Centre for Information Resilience.
The report described a campaign of systematic starvation and conflict‑related sexual violence in Sudan.
The Foreign Office said the sanctions would ensure the horrors at El Fasher are known worldwide.
Ed Miliband, the UK Foreign Secretary, said perpetrators must be held accountable and that external support to warring parties must end.
He also said the war has created a humanitarian catastrophe.
The UK allocated £5m to support survivors of sexual violence and £10m for humanitarian aid.
The targeted commanders include Hussein Abu Jalak, an RSF colonel linked to atrocities during the siege, and Al‑Nour Ahmed Adam, also known as Al‑Qubba.
Both were identified as playing prominent roles in the attack on El Fasher.
The sanctions cover individuals from both sides of the conflict.
Amnesty International reports that tens of thousands of civilians have been killed and 14 million people displaced since the war began in April 2023.
The fall of El Fasher was the largest and fastest civilian massacre in over 30 years.
The UK sanctions aim to address the ongoing violence and support survivors.
en.context: The city of El Fasher fell to RSF forces in 2025, triggering a siege that caused mass killings and sexual violence. The war in Sudan began in April 2023, leading to widespread displacement.
